extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedy writers and performers (stand-up, sketch, improv, roast, satire writers)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical template collection and how‑to guide for structuring comedic material across formats (stand‑up tight fives, one‑liners, sketch scripts, sitcom scenes, improv character cards, roasts, and satirical articles). Includes fillable fields, structure rules, and usage tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand‑Up Set Blueprint (Tight 5 Format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template fields: Title; Persona; Opener ([one‑sentence intro joke]); multiple Joke Clusters grouped by topic (each with Setup, Punchline, Tag, Callback prep); Callback to earlier joke; Closer ([big laugh line + emotional twist]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group your bits by theme. Build toward emotional vulnerability or total chaos. Test each cluster separately at open mics. Aim to 'leave them laughing and wanting more—not crying.' Use callback seeds in clusters and end with an emotional twist or big laugh line. (Metaphor: 'A tight five is like a first date. Leave them laughing and wanting more.')

rubrics_metrics.name: One‑Liner Writer's Grid
rubrics_metrics.description: Compact grid columns: Setup | Punchline | Tags. Example entries show a short setup with a surprising punchline and one‑word/short tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do 10 one‑liners per day; expect 'only 1 will be funny.' Treat comedy as volume work: 'Comedy = Rejection x Volume + Repetition².' Use tags to categorize/repurpose jokes and to spot patterns for callbacks or theme clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch Comedy Script Template
rubrics_metrics.description: Script format: TITLE; INT./LOCATION – TIME; list Characters; dialogue lines; stage directions like [Game established: ...]; BUTTON (final beat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch Structure: Premise = real setting + one absurd twist; Game = repeating the absurdity; Escalate the absurdity; End with a bang (a strong button) rather than a let‑down. Heighten the game throughout. Example provided: 'Emotional Support IRS Agent' where tax code is used as emotional therapy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch Structure (Premise/Game/Escalate/Button)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise structural rubric for sketches: establish a real setting with an absurd twist (premise), define the game (the repeating mechanism), escalate the stakes or absurdity, finish with a strong button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly mark where the game is established and how each beat heightens it. Avoid endings that fizzle—aim for a surprising or callback‑based button.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sitcom Scene Breakdown Sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Scene planner fields: Episode title; Setting; Characters (with short descriptors); Conflict; Goal; Turns (scene beats); Resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the planner to map the scene's objective and how beats/turns escalate the central conflict. Include a B‑plot or secondary beat for emotional layering to enrich the scene (example: haunted Keurig B‑plot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improv Character Bio Card
rubrics_metrics.description: Card fields: Name; Age; Profession; Status; Objective; Quirk (e.g., 'Only speaks in IKEA instruction metaphors').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bio to jump into any improv scene with strong, specific choices—'character is everything' when plot disappears. Quirks and clear objectives give teammates something to react to and create comedic impulses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roast Writing Scaffold
rubrics_metrics.description: Roast template: Target Name; Intro Joke; Physical Jab; Career Insult; Callback Joke; Closer. Stated rule: 'Roasts must be mean, clever, and just barely legal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance and proportions: 60% insults, 30% jokes, 10% plausible deniability. Use physical/career/character jabs plus callbacks; end with a closer that acknowledges affection (e.g., 'We love you...') to soften deniability. Aim for cleverness rather than gratuitous cruelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roast Tone & Structure Rule (60/30/10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit numeric guideline for roast content composition: 60% insults, 30% jokes, 10% plausible deniability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the split to pace a roast set—majority pointed insults, enough humor to land laughs, and some lines to plausibly excuse or humanize the target near the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical Article Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Article components: Absurd Headline; Subtitle; Byline (playful fake persona); Article flow: Fake but grounded facts; Public reaction (quotes from fake sources); Policy analysis via parody logic; A named quote (e.g., 'Chad'); Final irony twist + callback to headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the satire believable enough ('fake but grounded facts') to work as parody. Finish with an ironic twist that ties back to the headline. The page also advises ethical considerations (see separate 'punch up, not down' rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Downloadable Stand‑Up Skeleton (copy/paste template)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy/paste skeleton: Opener – [establish persona + first punchline]; Joke Cluster 1 – [theme, 3 jokes + 1 callback seed]; Joke Cluster 2 – [contrast topic]; Closer – [wildest, weirdest joke with callback].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as immediate fillable skeleton when drafting a tight set. The cluster approach encourages thematic grouping and callback planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downloadable Sketch Script Layout (copy/paste template)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple script layout: INT. [LOCATION] – [TIME]; CHARACTER A: [setup]; CHARACTER B: [absurd response]; [repeat game]; BUTTON: [surprise or callback].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minimalist format for fast sketch drafts; emphasizes game repetition and a clear button.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downloadable One‑Liner Grid Template (copy/paste template)
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank grid with columns for Setup | Punchline | Tags to record and sort one‑liners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the grid to batch‑produce and tag lines, making it easier to find callbacks or theme overlaps and to track which lines land in performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Callbacks and Tagging as Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Across templates: seed callbacks in early jokes, use tags to track related material, and deliberately call back to earlier lines in closers or buttons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan callback seeds in clusters, use tags in one‑liner grids to spot material to recycle, and employ callbacks in closers or buttons for payoff. Examples: 'Callback prep' in stand‑up clusters; 'Callback Joke' in roast; 'Final irony twist + callback' in satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing & Iteration: Try Material at Open Mics
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction to 'Test each cluster separately at open mics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterate based on audience response; test clusters individually before sewing them into a set. Treat open mics as labs for pruning, timing adjustments, and tag/callback validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Templates as Scaffolding — Adapt and Personalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta guidance: 'Use These. Abuse These. Then Write Your Own.' Templates are described as scaffolding or invisible foundations—not final forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with templates to organize chaos, then modify formats to fit your voice. 'Comedy is math with feelings'—use structure to discover personal rhythms, then evolve your own formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: Satire Should Punch Up, Not Down
rubrics_metrics.description: Implied ethical guideline (reinforced by related post titles): satire should 'punch up, not down' and 'keep it ethical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing satirical pieces or roasts, favor targets of power/privilege rather than vulnerable groups; avoid gratuitous cruelty. Check the site's 'Satire Punches Up, Not Down–Keep It Ethical' guidance for details.
